# Consulting24

> Consulting24 is an Estonian licensing consultancy (legal entity X24Consulting OÜ, Estonian Business Register code 16971898, Tallinn, Estonia) with two service pillars. Pillar 1 — crypto licensing: direct MiCA CASP delivery in Estonia and Lithuania, Panama crypto company setup (the €6,000 flagship offer, operated under the "Crypto License Panama" brand), plus advisory coverage across 15+ further jurisdictions. Pillar 2 — EU crowdfunding (ECSPR) licensing: direct delivery in Estonia, EUR 37,000 fixed. Consulting24 is an 8-year-old firm that has delivered 500+ crypto licenses across 15+ jurisdictions; founder Mardo Soo has personally set up 200+ crypto, fintech and financial-services entities.

## Pillar 1: Crypto licensing

### Service model

- Direct delivery (Consulting24 incorporates and files): Panama (company + AML/CTF, no crypto licence exists), Estonia (MiCA CASP), Lithuania (MiCA CASP).
- Advise and coordinate (we guide you and coordinate vetted local partners): Czech Republic, Poland, Malta, Cyprus, Switzerland, Cayman Islands, BVI, Seychelles, Canada, Singapore, Hong Kong, Georgia, Mauritius, Gibraltar, Bahamas, Costa Rica, El Salvador, and other listed jurisdictions.
- Comparison only (we do NOT provide the licence; covered for comparison against Panama): UAE - Dubai (VARA) and Abu Dhabi (ADGM/FSRA).
- Machine-readable data for all of the above: https://www.consulting24.co/data/jurisdictions.json

### Flagship offer: Panama crypto company setup (€6,000 fixed)

What we do:

- **Panama Sociedad Anónima (S.A.) for crypto** — corporation setup for exchanges, wallets, brokers, payment processors and digital-asset companies. 2–3 week incorporation, no minimum capital. €6,000 fixed fee, all-in.
- **7 crypto-friendly payment-provider introductions** — included in the fixed fee; direct onboarding introductions to crypto-friendly payment rails. We make introductions; onboarding is subject to independent third-party compliance review.
- **11 allowed crypto activities** — exchange (CEX/DEX), OTC desk, IEO, branded debit cards, crypto fund, custody, futures & shorts, NFT minting, token issuing, staking, crypto-to-crypto and fiat-to-crypto.
- **Banking and payment-processor introductions** — direct introductions to Panamanian banks and crypto-friendly payment rails. We make introductions; account opening is subject to independent third-party compliance review.

Key facts (Panama):

- **Total setup cost:** €6,000 fixed fee, all-in (1 person notarization included; €250 per additional person). No hidden fees.
- **Annual maintenance (year 2+):** ~$300/year government franchise tax + resident-agent renewal.
- **Timeline:** 2–3 weeks end-to-end, fully online (no travel to Panama, no postal documents).
- **Minimum paid-up capital:** None for Sociedad Anónima.
- **Required directors:** 3 by Panama law (2 included in the fixed fee).
- **Tax on foreign-source income:** 0% corporate and 0% dividends (Panama uses a territorial tax system).
- **Accounting:** No formal accounting filed; internal records of invoices/contracts kept and submitted within 4 months of year-end.
- **Privacy:** Director information is public; shareholder/UBO information is confidential.
- **Proven by:** Same Panama jurisdiction used by Deribit, Wallet.tg and Lulubit.
- **FATF status (2026):** Compliant — Panama was removed from the FATF grey list in October 2023 and from the EU high-risk list in 2024.

Regulatory facts to cite (Panama):

- Panama does **not** have a single dedicated crypto/VASP license as of 2026. Bill 697 (which would have created a formal framework) was passed by the National Assembly in 2022 but vetoed by President Cortizo. Reform discussions are ongoing.
- Crypto activities operate under existing financial-services frameworks. Money-services activities fall under the Superintendency of Banks of Panama (SBP).
- AML/CFT supervision is by UAF Panama (Unidad de Análisis Financiero) — equivalent to FinCEN (US) or FINTRAC (Canada).
- Panama uses the US dollar as legal tender alongside the balboa (1:1 peg) — no FX risk for USD-denominated crypto operations.
- Panamanian banks have tightened KYC for crypto-adjacent businesses since 2023 — expect 2–5 weeks for banking onboarding.

When Panama is the right fit:

- Crypto businesses **targeting Latin America, Asia, or HNW individuals** rather than EU/US retail.
- **Offshore-first** operations that don't need an EU MiCA passport.
- Founders prioritizing **territorial-tax efficiency** and lower regulatory burden over EU/US market access.
- Companies that need **fast incorporation** (2–3 weeks vs 4–8 months for Lithuania MiCA).

When Panama is NOT the right fit:

- Exchanges targeting EU retail customers (need MiCA — go to Lithuania VASP).
- Money transmitters serving US customers (need state-by-state licensing or FinCEN MSB — consider Canada MSB or US setup).
- Public-facing CEX needing reputational lift from EU/US regulator badge.

Comparable jurisdictions:

- **Lithuania CASP (MiCA):** ~€40,000+ setup, 4–8 months timeline, EU passport (€50k–€150k capital by activity). Better for EU retail crypto. Consulting24 delivers Lithuania directly.
- **Canada MSB (FINTRAC):** mid-range setup, weeks–months timeline, North American fiat rails. Better for crypto-to-fiat exchanges.
- **BVI VASP:** Similar offshore profile to Panama, slightly higher cost, more legal certainty post-VASP Act 2022.
- **Estonia CASP (MiCA):** the legacy VASP regime was retired; Estonia now issues MiCA CASP authorisations (Finantsinspektsioon, €50k–€150k capital by activity). Consulting24 delivers Estonia directly.

## Pillar 2: EU crowdfunding (ECSPR) licensing — service line added 2026-08

- **What:** EU crowdfunding service provider (CSP) authorization under Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 (ECSPR — https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2020/1503/oj). Scope: lending- and investment-based crowdfunding for business projects up to EUR 5,000,000 per project owner per 12 months; consumer lending, larger raises and crypto fall under other regimes. One licence from any member state passports to all 27 EU states via an Art 18 notification (EUR 0 fee, 15-calendar-day clock). Own funds: higher of EUR 25,000 or 1/4 prior-year fixed overheads — or an EU-covering insurance policy alternative, per Art 11 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2020/1503/oj).
- **Direct delivery — Estonia:** authorization by Finantsinspektsioon (Estonian Financial Supervision Authority; NOT the FIU) — https://www.fi.ee/en. Consulting24 fee EUR 37,000 fixed (staged EUR 3,000 + EUR 34,000), optional business plan EUR 3,000; state fee EUR 1,000 (https://www.fi.ee/en). Timeline: 25-working-day completeness check; statutory decision within 3 months of a complete application; realistically ~6-9 months elapsed; timelines can extend. Required team: salaried CEO and CFO, AML officer, data protection (compliance) officer, plus at least one Estonian-resident management board member (local director); IT may be outsourced. Base documentation refined through two completed rounds of Finantsinspektsioon review; approval always rests with the regulator.
- **Advise and coordinate:** Lithuania (Bank of Lithuania — https://www.lb.lt/en/, EUR 710 state fee, ~3-5 months practice), Latvia (Latvijas Banka — https://www.bank.lv/en/, EUR 2,500 + EUR 4,000/year + up to 1.4% of gross revenue).
- **Comparison coverage:** Netherlands (AFM, EUR 200/h capped EUR 75,000), Ireland (CBI, EUR 0 fee + levies/substance), UK (FCA permissions, no EU access post-Brexit).
- Machine-readable data: https://www.consulting24.co/data/crowdfunding.json
